summary.text: 大 is a whole-graph picture of a standing adult human. It is commonly used to mean “big” and “great”; “adult” is proposed as an earlier sense, though a dated sequence linking the two is lacking.

formation.text: Pictographic: the whole graph depicts a frontal human figure. Descriptions differ on whether the arms hang down or extend outward, so the pose is not settled; the figure’s interpretation does not depend on the popular outstretched-arms explanation.

components.text: The whole graph is analyzed as a frontal standing adult human, not as a combination of smaller signs. Descriptions differ on the arms’ position; the figure and its proposed original sense remain interpretations.

history.text: Historical sources label forms as oracle-bone, bronze, small-seal and standard script, describing the standard form as close to small seal. The curated oracle-bone, bronze and seal examples are modern redrawings that show broad stylistic differences, not a precise sequence of stroke changes.
An Eastern Han dictionary explanation says 大 depicts a human and records it as an ancient form of 亣. This is an early historical account of the graph, not independent proof of its prehistoric origin.

uncertainties.text: The earliest precisely dated use meaning “adult” or “big” is unresolved. A bronze inscription is cited for “big,” but its specific vessel and date are not established.

The proposed development from “adult” to “big” lacks a dated sequence of intermediate uses. The broad script labels likewise do not establish specific graphic changes, corruption or variant chronology.

senses.text: A specialist analysis proposes “adult,” contrasted with child, as an early sense; a precisely dated attestation for this use is unresolved.
A bronze inscription is cited using 大 for “big,” opposite 小; the specific vessel and date are unresolved.
大 is currently used with senses including “big,” “great,” “vast,” “large” and “high.”

developments.text: An analysis proposes that “big” developed from “adult,” but intermediate stages are not documented in a dated sequence.

limitations.text: The proposed adult-to-big development is an interpretation rather than a dated chain of attestations; the earliest precisely dated sense remains unresolved.
Modern glosses do not establish a historical sequence among “big,” “great,” “vast,” “large” and “high.”

items.period: Shang period style; the page identifies the script style, not a securely dated specimen in the SVG itself
items.caption: This modern redraw in Shang oracle-bone style shows 大 as a frontal figure with a long central body, arms extending sideways, and separated legs. The human-figure reading is supported, though accounts differ on the arms’ position.
items.alt: Black glyph with a long upright body, two sideways arms, and separated legs.
items.selection_reason: It gives a useful early-style example of the whole-graph human-figure analysis. The arms’ position remains disputed.

items.period: Early Western Zhou specimen is cited as a source; file depicts Western Zhou bronze-script style
items.caption: This modern redraw in Western Zhou bronze-script style shows a frontal figure with a tall central body, broad sideways arms, and legs below. It illustrates the script style; it does not identify a particular inscription or date a use of 大 for “big.”
items.alt: Black glyph with a tall central body, broad sideways arms, and two curved legs.
items.selection_reason: It adds a distinct bronze-script-style example. The redraw is not the inscription cited for the meaning “big.”

limitations.text: These modern redrawings show named script styles, not photographs of ancient objects. Accounts describe the human figure’s arms differently, and the glyphs alone cannot establish its original meaning or settle that disagreement.

The examples allow broad comparison across script styles, but do not establish a precise chronology of graphic changes or date the earliest use of 大. The proposed development from “adult” to “big” lacks a documented dated sequence of intermediate uses.
